analysis: Only the head text of .github/workflows/ci.yml was supplied (no base text or diff), so what changed is unknown. The visible content is CI job definitions. Third-party actions are SHA-pinned, with no pull_request_target and no secrets exposure. Some cache actions lack version comments, which is cosmetic only. Provider and coordinator test lanes add MiMo fixture preparation and nested-suite tripwires (run-nested-suite.sh). I found no new permissions, secrets or deploy steps. CHANGELOG.md is a patch (hunk +1,19) describing unreleased prefix-reuse work: demanded checkpoints, short-prefix capture, SSD write-share priority, and first-content token budgets. It also covers coordinator cache-holder matching that keeps the deepest compatible endpoint per provider and tier. No code was supplied for these, so none of it is verified. Relevant threat: T-041 (SSD prefix cache, SEC-035). Short-prefix capture and first-appearance SSD write access may loosen the per-donation adoption/benefit gate, which needs the T-041 sign-off checked. The reconcile-budget and cache-holder changes touch coordinator registry/cache routing. Later passes should confirm that cacheSalt account scoping (cache_route_keys.go) is unchanged and that holder-matching scratch overflow does not cross scopes. The remaining changelog statements are qualification-status notes with no visible security effect.

findings.detail: The changelog says an aligned demanded boundary is now captured "below the normal solo stripe, so repeated short prefixes can be published for reuse". It also says repeated checkpoints get the reserved SSD write share on first local appearance. T-041 records the encrypted SSD tier as signed off only for donations whose whole-block prefix exceeds the model's adoption bound plus the 1,024-token benefit floor. T-041's detection_hint says loosening that gate widens the at-rest surface and needs a fresh SEC-035 review. If this code lets sub-threshold prefixes reach SSDPrefixCache.donate, more at-rest artifacts are written and the same-account TTFT oracle extends to short prefixes. Only the changelog was supplied, so the actual gate behaviour is unverified. Fix: confirm that the SSD donation guard still applies to demanded short captures, or document the exception and refresh the T-041/SEC-035 sign-off.
findings.title: Changelog describes publishing short repeated prefixes to the SSD cache, outside the T-041 per-donation gate
